chapter: Art Blakey and the Jazz Messengers
title: Day-two clarifications: the Messengers' bassists and a North African country
summary: Brown corrects details from day one: George Tucker and Jymie Merritt as bassists in Blakey's band, and Golson cannot name the small Spanish-speaking place in North Africa.

bands.name: Art Blakey and the Jazz Messengers

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Great, great. In continuing this very enjoyable journey, I wanted to look back on some of the things that we had covered yesterday, but maybe fill in some of the blanks or the lapses that we had. For example, when you were talking about when Art Blakey re­ formed – got the Jazz Messengers together, pre- and post, there was some question about the bass player. I threw out Watkins, but I believe it was Doug Watkins. I went and researched it. Was he the bass player, the original bass player?

A little known fact. We had a bass player for a short while who played with Earl Bostic when I was there, named George Tucker, the late George Tucker. He was there for a short while. Then Jymie Merritt came later.
But Doug Watkins was the one that was with Horace Silver when Horace Silver was there.

Okay. I wanted to make sure that was clarified. You also said when you were in North Africa, you had been to Morocco, and we were trying to identify the other country. I believe it must have been Algeria?

It was up in the north. It wasn’t a country that we – that I didn’t know by name. It was strange, because they spoke Spanish. You leave that country, and you’re right out on the ocean. It was really the tip, north, right in the middle. I can’t think of what the name of that place was. They spoke Spanish, which was an aberration.

I thought maybe Algeria, because when I was looking at the map this morning, you got Morocco here, and then Algeria’s the next country, and it’s below – of course we know the French had gotten into Algeria, but it was below Spain too. So I tried the fact that maybe that was it, but we need to go further west on the Africa continent to identify where the country was at.
Yeah. It was small, a very small place.
